scope: Read-only diff of child lifetime binding, invoke exception cleanup, and unchanged oracle case/assertion suffix. No AST, native execution, process fault injection or timing run.
observations: Child preexec applies PR_SET_PDEATHSIG(SIGKILL) before exec and checks getppid against the parent PID captured before Popen; the parent-death race is covered.
Invoke encloses PTY setup/Popen/read/wait in finally, terminates and reaps the task-owned still-live child, closes both PTY descriptors, and saves captured PTY stdout on instrumentation failure.
Cleanup errors add notes to an in-flight original exception instead of replacing it; absent an original exception, cleanup failure still fails the test.

The prefix before child-lifetime setup and all code from compare() through case generation/result checks are byte-identical to the reviewed r1. Original 30s per-child timeout and separate OPEN handoff semantics remain.
Exceptional setup paths may have only preserved raw stdout/stderr and enclosing traceback rather than a complete process.json; no successful-process receipt is asserted on those paths.
remaining_limits: Static reasoning does not substitute for actual cleanup fault controls or eventual CI execution.
The direct-child guarantee applies to the frozen no-fork native entry and selected oracle paths; no arbitrary descendant-tree termination proof is claimed.
No product CLI or namespace closure claim is made.
